questions.topic: Beyond syllabus: GP terms, common ratio and sum to infinity
questions.question: The tenth term of a G.P. is 8 times its 13th term. The first term is 3. (a) Write the expression for 10th and 13th term. (b) Find the common ratio. (c) Find the sum up to infinite terms.
questions.solution: (a) T₁₀ = ar⁹ = 3r⁹ and T₁₃ = ar¹² = 3r¹². (b) ar⁹ = 8ar¹² ⇒ r³ = 1/8 ⇒ r = 1/2. (c) Since |r| < 1, S∞ = a/(1 − r) = 3/(1 − 1/2) = 6. (Sum to infinity is beyond the Class 10 syllabus; the key writes Sₙ = 6[1 − (1/2)ⁿ], which tends to 6.)

questions.question: Shown below is a horizontal water tank composed of a cylinder and two hemispheres (total length 34 m, diameter 14 m). The tank is filled up to a height of 7 m. Find (a) the surface area of the tank in contact with the water (b) the quantity of water that can be stored inside the horizontal water tank.
questions.solution: r = 7 m; cylinder length h = 34 − 14 = 20 m. Water fills up to 7 m = half the tank. (a) Wetted area = ½(2πrh) + ½(4πr²) = πrh + 2πr² = πr(h + 2r) = (22/7) × 7 × (20 + 14) = 22 × 34 = 748 m². (b) Water in the tank = ½(πr²h + 4/3 πr³) = ½((22/7) × 49 × 20 + (4/3)(22/7) × 343) = ½(3080 + 1437.33) = 2258.67 m³. (Full capacity of the tank = 4517.33 m³.)

questions.question: Two people standing on the same side of a tower in a straight line with it, measures the angles of elevation of the top of the tower as 25° and 50° respectively. If the height of the tower is 70m, find the distance between the two people.
questions.solution: Let AB = 70 m be the tower, C and D the people with elevations 25° and 50°. BC = 70 cot 25° = 70 tan 65° = 70 × 2.1445 = 150.12 m. BD = 70 cot 50° = 70 tan 40° = 70 × 0.8391 = 58.74 m. CD = 150.12 − 58.74 = 91.38 ≈ 91.4 m.

(b) Construct the locus of all points equidistant from A and B. (c) Mark the point which satisfies both the conditions (a) and (b) as P. Hence, construct a circle with centre P and passing through A and B.
questions.solution: Draw AB = 6 cm. At B construct 75° (bisect between 60° and 90°) and cut BC = 5 cm. (a) The locus of points equidistant from AB and BC is the bisector of ∠ABC — construct it. (b) The locus of points equidistant from A and B is the perpendicular bisector of AB — construct it. (c) Their intersection is P. questions.topic: Double inequation over integers on number line
questions.question: Solve the following inequation and represent the solution set on the number-line. −3 + x ≤ 8x/3 + 2 ≤ 14/3 + 2x ; x ∈ I
questions.solution: −3 + x ≤ 8x/3 + 2 ⇒ −9 + 3x ≤ 8x + 6 ⇒ −15 ≤ 5x ⇒ x ≥ −3. 8x/3 + 2 ≤ 14/3 + 2x ⇒ 8x + 6 ≤ 14 + 6x ⇒ x ≤ 4. So −3 ≤ x ≤ 4, x ∈ I: solution set {−3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4}, shown as solid dots at these integers on the number line.

questions.question: If a, b and c are in continued proportion, then prove that: 1/a³ + 1/b³ + 1/c³ = a/(b²c²) + b/(a²c²) + c/(a²b²).
questions.solution: a, b, c in continued proportion ⇒ b² = ac. RHS = (a³ + b³ + c³)/(a²b²c²) = (a³ + b³ + c³)/(a²c² · ac) = (a³ + b³ + c³)/(a³c³) = 1/c³ + b³/(a³c³) + 1/a³. Since a³c³ = (ac)³ = b⁶, b³/(a³c³) = 1/b³. So RHS = 1/a³ + 1/b³ + 1/c³ = LHS.

questions.topic: Selling and reinvesting shares, change in income
questions.question: Ravi sells a certain number of Rs 20 shares paying 8 % dividend at Rs 18 and invested the proceeds in Rs 10 shares paying 12 % dividend at 50 % premium. If the change in his annual income is Rs 120, find the number of shares sold by Ravi.
questions.solution: Let x shares be sold. Old income = x × 8% of 20 = 1.6x = 8x/5. Proceeds = 18x. New MV = 10 + 5 = ₹15, new shares = 18x/15 = 1.2x; new income = 1.2x × 12% of 10 = 1.44x = 36x/25. Change: 8x/5 − 36x/25 = 4x/25 = 120 ⇒ x = 750 shares.

questions.question: Use the ogive to answer the questions below: (a) the median marks (b) Number of students scoring more than or equal to 50 but less than 70 marks. (c) Number of students who got atleast 75 marks. (d) The upper quartile range (e) The total number of students. [Ogive: marks on x-axis (2 cm = 10 marks), number of students on y-axis (2 cm = 10 students), through (0, 0), (10, 2), (20, 5), (30, 11), (40, 21), (50, 41), (60, 63), (70, 73), (80, 80).]
questions.solution: N = 80. (a) Median = (N/2)th = 40th student → about 49 marks (interpolation gives 49.5). (b) cf at 70 − cf at 50 = 73 − 41 = 32 students. (c) cf at 75 ≈ 77, so students with at least 75 marks ≈ 80 − 77 = 3. (d) Upper quartile Q₃ = (3N/4)th = 60th student → about 59 marks; lower quartile Q₁ = 20th student → about 39 marks; interquartile range = 59 − 39 = 20 marks. (e) Total students = 80.

questions.topic: Intra-state supply chain: SGST, CGST, final price
questions.question: A product is sold from P to Q for Rs 8000 and then from Q to R. If the rate of tax under GST is 18 % and the profit made by Q is Rs 3000, find: (a) the GST paid by Q to State Government (b) the GST received by Central Government (c) the total price paid by R.
questions.solution: SP of Q = 8000 + 3000 = ₹11000. CGST = SGST = 9%. (a) Q pays SGST on its value addition: 9% of 3000 = ₹270. (b) Central Government receives CGST 9% of 11000 = ₹990 (₹720 from P + ₹270 from Q). (c) Price paid by R = 11000 + 18% of 11000 = 11000 + 1980 = ₹12980.

questions.question: If x = (√(a + 1) + √(a − 1))/(√(a + 1) − √(a − 1)), then using the properties of proportion show that: x² − 2ax + 1 = 0
questions.solution: By componendo and dividendo, (x + 1)/(x − 1) = 2√(a + 1)/2√(a − 1) = √(a + 1)/√(a − 1). Squaring: (x + 1)²/(x − 1)² = (a + 1)/(a − 1). Again by componendo and dividendo: [(x + 1)² + (x − 1)²]/[(x + 1)² − (x − 1)²] = 2a/2 ⇒ (2x² + 2)/(4x) = a ⇒ x² + 1 = 2ax ⇒ x² − 2ax + 1 = 0.

questions.question: Prove the identity: cos⁶A + sin⁶A = 1 − 3cos²A sin²A
questions.solution: LHS = (cos²A)³ + (sin²A)³ = (cos²A + sin²A)(cos⁴A + sin⁴A − cos²A sin²A) = 1 × [(cos²A + sin²A)² − 2cos²A sin²A − cos²A sin²A] = 1 − 3cos²A sin²A = RHS.

questions.question: The difference of the square of two natural numbers is 84. The square of the larger number is 25 times the smaller number. Taking x to be the smaller number, form a quadratic equation in x and solve it to find numbers.
questions.solution: Let the larger number be y: y² − x² = 84 and y² = 25x. So 25x − x² = 84 ⇒ x² − 25x + 84 = 0 ⇒ (x − 4)(x − 21) = 0 ⇒ x = 4 or 21. If x = 21, y² = 525 is not a perfect square (and y < x), so reject. x = 4, y² = 100, y = 10. The numbers are 4 and 10.

questions.topic: Pole on tower: elevation and depression
questions.question: Draw the necessary diagram for this question. A pole 6m high is fixed on the top of a tower. The angle of elevation of the top of the pole observed from a point P on the ground is 60° and the angle of depression of the point P from the top of the tower is 45°. Find the height of the tower and the distance of point P from the foot of the tower.
questions.solution: Let AB = h be the tower, AE = 6 m the pole, B the foot. Depression 45° from A ⇒ ∠APB = 45°, so PB = AB = h. In ΔEPB: tan 60° = (h + 6)/h ⇒ √3h = h + 6 ⇒ h = 6/(√3 − 1) = 3(√3 + 1) = 3 × 2.732 = 8.196 ≈ 8.20 m. Height of tower ≈ 8.20 m and distance PB ≈ 8.20 m.
